title: O*NET 31.0 Database: Work Styles, Essential Skills, Transferable Skills, Career Interest Types, Occupation Data, Content Model Reference
publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (USDOL/ETA), National Center for O*NET Development
attribution: This page includes information from the O*NET 31.0 Database by the U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (USDOL/ETA). Used under the CC BY 4.0 license. O*NET® is a trademark of USDOL/ETA. Foothold has modified all or some of this information. USDOL/ETA has not approved, endorsed, or tested these modifications.
modifications: Work Styles WI values (-3..+3) converted to 0..1 percentile ranks across all occupations with complete Work Styles data (traits.json ids, occupations.json, careers.json).
Element names mapped to snake_case ids; Work Styles and skill descriptions copied verbatim from content_model_reference.csv.
Career skill lists choose the 5 O*NET skills with the highest Importance relative to the all-occupation mean, combined with Foothold job-specific skills.
Only 42 of the 1,016 occupations are kept in occupations.json (8 Foothold careers + 34 related occupations).
Foothold career titles and summaries are Foothold's own; O*NET titles are kept in onet_title.

methods.Work styles (traits) on a 0..1 scale: For each of the 21 O*NET 31.0 Work Styles and each occupation: value = (number of occupations with a lower Work Styles Impact (WI) + 0.5 x number with the same WI) / 891, where 891 is every O*NET-SOC occupation with complete Work Styles data (21 elements, WI and DR). 0.5 is about the middle of all occupations; 0.9 means a higher WI than about 90% of occupations. Raw WI and DR stay in occupations.json.
methods.Career skills: careers.json skills = Foothold job-specific skills (editorial, SAMPLE) + the 5 O*NET 31.0 skills with the highest Importance z-score versus the mean of all 910 occupations with Skills data, among skills with Importance >= 2.5.
